BQS.confidence: Medium descriptive quality; not ranking eligible untilG2 resolved

GQS.confidence: Medium descriptive quality; not ranking eligible untilG2 resolved

IAS.override: IAS NS underG2; no artificial cap substituted

GOV.rationale: No evidenced diversion/default or abusive minority action. However repeated internally unmatched audit EOM references, poorly explained advances, sizeable technology capital and family transactions prevent an ordinary clean-governance score. Clean opinion/IFC and disclosed restatement are positive counterevidence.
GOV.counterevidence: Unmodified audit and IFC opinions, positive audit-trail reporting, no reported default or fraud, and a disclosed FY2024 restatement bridge argue against a severe integrity-failure classification.

MOAT.rationale: Network of lenders/referrers and execution capability has value, but concentration, commission sharing, non-exclusive products and readily available direct channels constrain pricing power. CRM spend alone does not prove proprietary advantage.
MOAT.counterevidence: The company reports over70 lender partners and5,000 referral agents; falling top-ten customer concentration supports some distribution breadth despite non-exclusive access.

REV.rationale: Five-year organic revenue CAGR56.94% maps to9, capped8 for medium confidence in like-for-like commission mix and no throughput/take-rate bridge. Three-year29.96% independently maps8. FY26 growth46.01% and retained growth36.34% support acceleration; no extra trajectory point.
REV.counterevidence: FY2025 growth slowed to13.07% and FY2026 retained growth lagged gross revenue; missing take-rate/volume decomposition limits certainty despite strong audited growth.

DUR.rationale: Credit distribution access and new cross-selling offer several years of runway, but lender appetite, commission economics, agent churn and regulatory dependence constrain visibility; no 10-year market-share extrapolation.
DUR.counterevidence: Insurance has already reached approximately5% of revenue and lending-partner access supports cross-selling; conversely recurring renewal/trail economics are not yet established for the whole business.

CAP.rationale: Conservative stable-perimeter incremental capital bridge: FY23–FY26 post-tax operating-profit increase₹8.7950 crore on₹52.0276 crore added invested capital gives16.90%; FY24–26 only9.34%. Include all CRM and unidentified advances rather than inventing asset-light economics. Recovery risk and accelerating reinvestment prevent a high score, but audited multi-year bridge supports a bounded score rather than NS for absent cohorts.
CAP.counterevidence: The stable organic bridge does support a positive16.90% three-year incremental return, not merely growth without returns; the recent two-year9.34% and unreconciled advance recoverability prevent a high score.

CASH.rationale: Persistent weak conversion across five audited years, negative cumulative FCF and continuing advance/CRM outlays. Three-year statutory and restated-chain alternatives reach same conclusion. This is not explained away as one seasonal build. Applies GQS cap5.
CASH.counterevidence: CFO remains positive in the latest four years and some expansion expenditure may eventually mature. However five-year conversion21.95% and both statutory/restated three-year alternatives prevent treating this as a single transient build.

BAL.rationale: Positive₹65.4158 crore book equity and no reported debt default provide support. ₹7.3559 crore demand cash does not equal₹14.8719 crore reported bank/FD, nearly full revolver,₹3.3228 crore current term maturities and weak conversion constrain resilience. Not classified insolvent from a chosen reserve threshold.
BAL.counterevidence: Reported total bank/cash/deposits exceed gross debt and no default is reported. FD availability could fund the base; deposits are excluded conservatively rather than assumed worthless.

EXEC.rationale: Revenue scale, new insurance/MF permissions and product launch are delivered, while CRM stays under development, initial debt repayment is followed by rising debt and commission payout rises. Recent WTD turnover and cash realization lower confidence in conversion of growth to owner value.
EXEC.counterevidence: Product permissions, insurance revenue and revenue scale are delivered. Capital still parked in CRM and recurring advance absorption weaken the economic-delivery evidence.

EARN.rationale: Operating EBIT rose, but gross payout inflation and unamortized software make PAT growth a less clean measure. Five-year amortization of existing CRM reduces FY26 PAT proxy from₹12.0033 crore to₹10.0081 crore before other adjustments.
EARN.counterevidence: Operating EBIT increased materially and IPO restatement is disclosed; normalization risk is about amortization/recoverability and cash realization, not a claim that all earnings are fictitious.

R.rationale: Ordinary IRR withheld under unresolved G2 and uncertain cash trajectory. A conditionally funded bull or hypothetical rescue return is not a base-case investment return.
R.counterevidence: Full FD availability can produce a funded base and a favorable conditional return; hypothetical prefunding also closes arithmetic gaps. These assumptions do not remove G2 or prove financing availability.

D.rationale: No-lender-credit-book structure and equity cushion reduce direct default exposure, but advance/CRM impairment, weaker lender conversion, payout pressure and thin execution create meaningful permanent-loss mechanisms. Bear no-rescue path fails funding; hypothetical diluted rescue remains loss-making.
D.counterevidence: No customer loan-book underwriting exposure, positive book equity and no reported debt default are real protections; advance/CRM impairment and financing/exit friction remain meaningful loss channels.

P.rationale: Current P/E looks low, but investor expectations cannot be scored confidently against unverified normalized earnings and a conditional base funding path. No peer-multiple shortcut.
P.counterevidence: Reported9.36x P/E and approximately1.72x book value could leave upside if cash realization improves. Incomplete earnings/cash reliability still prevents a supportable expectation score.

L.rationale: 55/60 authenticated issuer rows are insufficient to label five absent sessions zero or establish a full-window distribution. Strict lot-constrained5% participation is below one lot on observed median. Depth/spread/circuit-sale feasibility ND.
L.counterevidence: 55 actual trading rows show active trading, and observed20-day10% participation permits one lot per session. Five missing60-day statuses and absent spread/depth still preclude a validated full-window exit score.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. My Mudra is an organically growing distributor of financial products, not a lender funding a loan book. Revenue reached ₹117.34 crore in FY2026 and grew at 29.96% annually over FY2023–FY2026. However, FY2026 CFO was only ₹2.06 crore against ₹12.00 crore PAT, while advances and technology development absorbed substantial capital. At ₹98.65, reported P/E of 9.36× looks inexpensive, but earnings have not translated into distributable cash. A material audit emphasis-of-matter reference remains unresolved. This is a distribution-growth/value watchlist thesis, not an established compounder. A quantified bank reconciliation, recoverable advances, technology commissioning and sustainable cash conversion could change the conclusion. A lower price alone would not resolve the financial-reliability hold.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: My Mudra Fincorp Limited: NSE Emerge MYMUDRA; ISIN INE0RVQ01016; CIN L65191DL2013PLC257611. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026; latest audited balance sheet is 31 March 2026. The official 19 October close is ₹98.65, giving market capitalization of ₹112.380107 crore on 11,391,800 shares. Accounts are standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not consolidated Ind AS lender accounts. The September 2025 limited-review half-year is historical, not a September 2026 update. Horizon: 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, exactly 1,826 days; nominal pretax INR equity hurdle 15%, with 12% and 18% sensitivities; liquidity reference position ₹500,000. Gates: G1 Conditional, G2 Hold — unresolved, G3 Conditional and G4 Conditional. Confidence is High in identified primary-source rows, Medium in descriptive growth/capital comparisons and Low in investment conclusions while G2 remains unresolved. An unmodified opinion is important counterevidence, but not a substitute for explaining the EOM.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: All 13 factors, evidence references and exact weighted contributions are shown below. BQS is 4.76 unrounded and 4.8 displayed. GQS raw 6.10 is capped at 5.0 because CASH scores 2 for persistent weak realization. IAS is NS, with 45% evidence-weight coverage and a missing-data bound rather than a point estimate. Its quality contribution uses 4.76, not the rounded 4.8. REV is capped at 8 under Medium confidence. Numerical BQS/GQS are descriptive diagnostics and are excluded from rankings until the material G2 issue is resolved. Neither a governance-failure nor a funding-failure cap is imposed: severe misconduct and unavoidable funding failure have not been established.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: My Mudra earns commissions from banks, NBFCs and other product providers for sourcing and distributing financial products. It shares revenue with referral partners, then pays employee, processing, technology and other operating costs. Its revenue is fee income, not loan disbursement principal, AUM, premium or deposits. FY2026 commission expense of ₹82.2651 crore leaves ₹35.0767 crore before employee and other expenses. Approximate product mix was business loans 36%, personal loans 34%, loan against property 18%, home loans 5%, professional loans 2% and insurance 5%. Management reports over 70 bank/NBFC partners, 5,000 digital referral agents, 165 branches and 244 employees. These are company-reported network measures, not proof that all locations are owned or equally productive. There was no subsidiary at March 2026. The proposed payments subsidiary is a later proposal, not an established profit contributor. Direct loan underwriting losses are not modeled as though My Mudra were the lender; lender risk appetite, commission clawbacks, customer complaints and compliance can nevertheless affect collections.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The plausible advantage is localized lead generation, lender/referral relationships and processing execution. Data and integrations may improve conversion, but competing DSAs and direct channels can offer the same products. The prospectus reports top-ten customer concentration of 63.56% in FY2024, down from 77.97% in FY2023 and 84.79% in FY2022. This is improving diversification, not low concentration. Retained commission share declined from approximately 32.01% in FY2025 to 29.89% in FY2026. Three primary-source comparators illuminate different mechanisms: PB Fintech/Paisabazaar for digital credit and insurance sourcing, Prudent for wealth distribution and recurring trail economics, and private NJ Wealth for partner-network scale. None is an interchangeable valuation comparable. No current peer P/E or market value has been invented. A higher moat score would require demonstrated retention, repeat conversion, take-rate resilience and returns after customer/partner acquisition costs.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: The five-year revenue CAGR uses six observations: FY2021 ₹12.32306 crore to FY2026 ₹117.3418 crore, or 56.94% annually. FY2023–FY2026 CAGR is 29.96%. Annual revenue growth was 88.36%, 32.95%, 13.07% and 46.01% in FY2023–FY2026 respectively. FY2026 added ₹36.9766 crore of revenue. Retained commission grew from ₹13.7219 crore in FY2023 to ₹35.0767 crore in FY2026, a 36.73% CAGR; its FY2026 growth of 36.34% lagged headline growth as partner payouts increased. No acquisition was located within the reviewed standalone perimeter; insurance cross-selling is an organic extension. Loan disbursement volume, take-rate and active-partner cohort data are ND, so organic growth is not assumed to mean volume alone. H1 FY2026 revenue was ₹58.4474 crore versus ₹33.7388 crore, up approximately 73.23%; H2 was ₹58.8944 crore versus ₹46.6264 crore, up 26.31%. The second half slowed but still grew. No half-year is mislabeled as a quarter or annualized into a forecast.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Credit demand and access outside major cities offer runway, but a bottom-up growth path needs productive agents, lender approvals, retained commissions and collected fees, not simply branch counts. The business is asset-light only in the narrow sense of not financing customer loans: ₹13.3011 crore of CRM development and ₹25.4153 crore of other advances are material capital at risk. A conservative, stable-perimeter incremental capital bridge gives 16.90% post-tax incremental ROIC for FY2023–FY2026, 9.34% for FY2024–FY2026 and 14.77% for FY2026 alone. All unidentified advances and CRM capital remain in the denominator. This supports a bounded CAP score of 5, rather than declaring it NS because private cohort data are unavailable. It does not establish recoverability. IPO proceeds were fully used by March 2026, so recurring capex and advances remain in forecasts. The GQS cap of 5.0 deliberately separates rapid sales growth from weak growth in cash available to owners. A judgmental nominal INR operating cost-of-capital range of 12–15%, distinct from the 15% equity-return hurdle, recognizes a small distributor with expensive unsecured debt, concentration and thin shares. The 16.90% three-year incremental return is only modestly above that range; 9.34% for the latest two years is below it. This range is a sensitivity benchmark, not a falsely precise observed WACC.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters held 6,594,400 shares, or 57.8873%, at March 2026 versus 57.8346% a year earlier. Pledge percentage at the cutoff is ND and is not inferred to be zero. Disclosed FY2026 related-party transactions include ₹0.50 crore of director advances given and repaid, remuneration of ₹0.30 crore each to the MD and Nisha Kulshrestha, and ₹0.0991 crore of commission to the MD's brother. They require commercial-purpose and recovery scrutiny, not an automatic allegation of abuse. CARO reports no debt default, wilful default or fraud; IFC and audit-trail findings are positive. Disputed tax/GST exposure is ₹0.9272 crore. Some statutory payments were delayed, but no undisputed amount overdue more than six months was reported. Whole-time director turnover includes Abhisek Dhal on 26 March 2026 and Madan Sardar on 9 October 2026 after an August appointment; the latter cites personal reasons and no other material reason. The decisive reliability issue is more specific: the FY2026 EOM directs readers to CARO ii(b) for material differences between quarterly bank statements and books, but that clause gives no differences and says reporting is not required. FY2024 and FY2025 show the same pair, so the annual-report disclosure issue spans three years. A template error is possible, not verified. Quantified reconciliation or an auditor-signed correction is needed; this is a hold, not a fraud finding.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: The historical tables preserve basis differences. FY2022–FY2024 use IPO-restated standalone accounts; FY2025–FY2026 use audited statutory accounts with the same operating perimeter. Parallel statutory FY2024 figures prevent a silent splice. Statutory PAT ₹6.4259 crore becomes restated ₹8.3552 crore through a disclosed ₹1.9293 crore bridge, dominated by ₹1.925 crore of prior-period expense reallocation. FY2026 operating EBITDA of ₹18.579 crore excludes ₹0.4521 crore other income; operating EBIT is ₹17.0401 crore and PAT ₹12.0033 crore. CFO of ₹2.0614 crore less ₹8.1535 crore cash capex is negative ₹6.0921 crore, before ₹1.3516 crore financing interest and ₹2.5292 crore long-term advance outflow. Reported CFO includes interest income and classifies interest paid under financing, so CFO minus capex is not FCFE. Receivables of ₹20.9089 crore represent approximately 65.04 closing days and are mostly recent; generic advances lack an equivalent ageing schedule. CRM development grew from ₹1.2213 crore in FY2023 to ₹13.3011 crore without a clearly identified ready-for-use transfer. Five-year incremental amortization lowers the PAT proxy by ₹1.9952 crore; three- and seven-year alternatives are shown. Tax provision is explicitly net of advance tax/TDS. The separate generic revenue-authority balance is therefore not assumed to offset it or be immediately refundable. Legacy tax, statutory, interest and gratuity amounts settle once in the cash model; trade working capital is separately reconciled. Book equity is not a liquid liquidation value.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹98.65, market capitalization is ₹112.380107 crore. Mechanical reported P/E is 9.36×, five-year CRM-amortization PAT-proxy P/E 11.23× and price/book approximately 1.72×. EV excluding unverified FD availability is ₹116.287607 crore, or 6.82× operating EBIT. Full reported-cash EV is explicitly a sensitivity, not verified unrestricted cash. Bear/base/bull use revenue growth of 3%/15%/25%, EBITDA margins 10%/14.5%/17%, receivable days 100/75/62, recurring capex 5.5%/4.5%/4% and terminal EV/EBIT of 7×/10×/12×. These are analyst assumptions, not peer facts. Quarterly cash rows run from March 2026 through the exact entry and terminal dates. Core paths exclude FD release and generic revenue-authority recovery; all breach the ₹3 crore buffer, including before entry. Base eventually has negative cash. This is not an observed default: access to the existing ₹7.5159 crore FDs can change feasibility, and the full-release alternative is shown separately. Unfunded paths have no no-rescue IRR. Hypothetical prefunding uses an issue price equal to 80% of the reference price, 2% fees and whole shares rounded up; base and bear exceed current authorized share capacity and require approvals/capital expansion. Ordinary returns and actionable entry prices remain NS under G2. Fully funded contingent paths alone may support reverse-multiple solutions and 12%/15%/18% hurdle values. No unfunded solver endpoint is presented as success.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest counterargument to cheap growth is that rising revenue may require permanent advance funding and underrecognized technology costs. Softer lender approvals can combine with lower retained commissions, slower collections and continued development spending. The bear case links 3% growth, a 10% EBITDA margin, 100 receivable days, 5.5% recurring capex and payment of the ₹0.9272 crore disputed exposure. It breaches the cash floor before entry; silently assuming a rescue would invalidate the return. A separate revolver-recall stress repays ₹4.9925 crore and worsens the shortfall. Fully prefunded hypothetical bear rescue produces an approximately negative 9.46% annualized outcome at the reference entry price, with owner dilution, but no such financing has been approved or received. Permanent loss may also arise through advance/CRM impairment rather than a temporary valuation multiple change. The thesis-break variable is cash after ongoing reinvestment, not reported PAT growth alone.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five- or ten-fold returns are not the central thesis. Across the exact 1,826-day horizon, 5× and 10× price appreciation require approximately 38.0% and 58.5% annualized returns. At unchanged shares and a 10× terminal operating EBIT multiple, temporarily ignoring net financial claims for this rough feasibility test, five times today's capitalization needs about ₹56.2 crore EBIT and ten times needs ₹112.4 crore, versus FY2026 EBIT of ₹17.04 crore. That implies approximately 27% and 46% annual EBIT growth over five years before reinvestment and dilution. Strong bull operating assumptions can mathematically generate more than 5× in a fully funded contingent path, but the calculation neither establishes its probability nor validates the financial inputs. A 10× outcome needs even stronger sustained economics, favorable valuation or both. No target or probability is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor the next available half-year and annual filing rather than inventing quarterly cash accounts. Priorities are the bank/EOM reconciliation; rolling CFO/PAT and cash after all capital needs; counterparty ageing and recovery of ₹25.4153 crore other advances; CRM commissioning and amortization; FD liens/maturities, debt service and unused facilities; retained commission share; productive partners and product mix; dilution and authorized capital; and lot-constrained exit conditions. The table gives baselines and escalation thresholds. A coherent dated cash bridge can resolve funding uncertainty without a universal demand for daily bank statements, but the explicit audit conflict needs its own explanation. This is a research monitoring plan, not a scheduled automation, trade instruction or communication to management.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Final classification: Hold — unresolved, distribution-growth/value watchlist. BQS 4.8 and capped GQS 5.0 describe the available evidence but do not place the company in an investable ranking while financial reliability is material. IAS is NS and no actionable entry range is supplied. Neither 'avoid because of proven fraud' nor 'distressed because failure is established' is supported. The shares are not necessarily expensive: reported multiples are low, and real improvement in cash realization could produce substantial value. Price cannot, however, resolve unknown asset recoverability and bank-statement differences. For new money, evidence comes before a target price. An existing holder must also consider position size and exit friction; those personal circumstances were not provided. A clean reconciliation, documented advance collection, CRM commissioning and a funded growth path would permit an updated IAS and conditional valuation.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual reports FY2022–FY2026, the final prospectus, audited FY2026 results, H1 FY2026 limited-review results and dated September/October 2026 announcements were reviewed, including audit annexures. The official NSE 19 October security master and 60 validated daily bhavcopies anchor market data. Five absent issuer rows remain unclassified, not zero volume. Official competitor pages support business mechanisms only, not valuation multiples. The ledger, hashes, evidence IDs, extracted numbers, definitions and source-safe deterministic builders accompany the report. Raw filings and indiscriminate OCR containing personal identifiers are excluded from shareable archives. F denotes reported fact, C calculation and A assumption; forecast cash rows are assumptions, not observed current bank balances. Open items are a quantified EOM/CARO explanation, advance purposes and ageing, FD availability, CRM readiness/useful life, current cash/debt movements and complete absent-session status. Historical restatements and rounding differences are retained rather than selected to improve a thesis. No external outreach, publication or trade was undertaken by this research task.

Income-tax provision is reported net of advance tax/TDS. No generic revenue-authority balance is assumed realized in the core path; contingent recovery and timing are sensitivity-only. Undisbursed credit limit only ₹0.0075 crore, not added. All FD balances excluded absent lien/maturity confirmation; full-release sensitivity is contingent, not an authenticated receipt. Entry and terminal surplus are signed after reserve. Original CRM amortized, recurring digital/branch capex continues after IPO budget. No original-advance recovery added to equity EV. The ₹3 crore nominal reserve is an analyst minimum, not a contractual covenant; ₹0/₹1/₹5 crore sensitivity is supplied. Terminal earnings multiple assumes a mature business whose reinvestment remains within recurring capex, not a second five-year high-growth perpetuity. Legacy tax is front-loaded as conservative timing, not a claim of actual quarterly payment. New WOS ₹0.05 crore subscription remains wholly-owned group cash, not external acquisition spending; costs must fit operating/capex budget. Exact daily horizon excludes post-terminal cash.

summary: Hold — unresolved. My Mudra is an organically growing distributor of financial products, not a lender funding a loan book. Revenue reached ₹117.34 crore in FY2026 and grew at 29.96% annually over FY2023–FY2026. However, FY2026 CFO was only ₹2.06 crore against ₹12.00 crore PAT, while advances and technology development absorbed substantial capital. At ₹98.65, reported P/E of 9.36× looks inexpensive, but earnings have not translated into distributable cash. A material audit emphasis-of-matter reference remains unresolved. This is a distribution-growth/value watchlist thesis, not an established compounder. A quantified bank reconciliation, recoverable advances, technology commissioning and sustainable cash conversion could change the conclusion. A lower price alone would not resolve the financial-reliability hold.
